title: Classify Who Chooses the Next Step
summary: Distinguish model calls, deterministic workflows, agents, and agentic systems by executable control flow and feedback.
objectives: Trace code-directed and model-directed transitions separately.
Identify the loop, feedback, state, stop conditions, and controller.
Explain why tool-call output does not by itself create an agent.
Choose the least complex accurate classification.

sections.title: A model call produces an output
paragraphs: A model can generate an answer, plan, or tool-call proposal without controlling an executable loop. The caller still decides what happens next. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

Tool-call syntax describes a requested action. An authorized runtime must validate arguments, resolve the target, execute or refuse the call, and return evidence. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

sections.title: A deterministic workflow follows predefined transitions
paragraphs: Code or configuration selects the next step in a deterministic workflow. A model may generate or classify inside a step while the workflow remains the controller. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

Deterministic does not mean perfectly predictable output. It means the executable path and transition authority are defined outside the model. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

sections.title: An agent chooses among permitted next steps
paragraphs: A bounded agent pursues a goal through a loop: observe state, choose an allowed action, receive feedback, update state, and continue or stop. External controls still own identity, authority, budgets, verification, and terminal outcomes. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

An agentic system is the complete operating boundary around one or more agents: harness, tools, state, policy, telemetry, evaluation, approvals, recovery, and accountable people. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

sections.title: Multiple calls are not multiple agents
paragraphs: A multi-agent system has separately instructed or controlled agent units that coordinate, delegate, or hand off work through explicit contracts. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

Parallel requests, debate prompts, or multiple models do not prove multi-agent behavior unless separate responsibilities and coordination are observable. questions.prompt: What most directly distinguishes an agent loop from a deterministic workflow?
choices: A model chooses among permitted next steps from feedback
The workflow contains more than one step
The provider uses the word agent
questions.explanation: Model-directed next-step selection within a bounded feedback loop is the distinguishing control signal.

questions.prompt: A model returns a function name and arguments. What has happened?
choices: The model proposed a tool call; execution still belongs to a runtime
questions.explanation: A proposal is not execution, authorization, or postcondition evidence.

questions.prompt: A fixed pipeline calls a model in step two. How should it be classified?
choices: A deterministic workflow if code still selects transitions
Unknown because models cannot appear in workflows
questions.explanation: Model use does not change who controls the executable path.

choices: Separate agent responsibilities plus observable coordination or handoffs
questions.explanation: Multiple agents require distinct controlled units and coordination evidence.

questions.prompt: What is the preferred design when a fixed workflow meets every requirement?
questions.explanation: Use the least complex design that satisfies the evidence and operating requirements.
